title: Quentin and the Veil
premise: Ines Okafor has spent his life as the reluctant keeper of the Hollow Gate in a valley where magic cannot follow, guarding a seal that ended an ancient war. When his charming new date, Quentin, turns out to be named in a century-old prophecy as the one who will either renew or destroy the Veil, Ines must smuggle him past the valley's wards and into a world of exiled mages who want Quentin as their weapon. As factions hunt them and the moon wanes toward its thirteenth turn, Ines discovers the prophecy was forged by the gate's first keepers to lure a vessel for the sealed power itself. In the end, Ines and Quentin—now bound by found family among outcasts—shatter the prophecy rather than fulfill it, sealing the power not behind a gate but within a chosen circle of guardians, at the cost of the valley's magicless sanctuary forever.
about_author: Hazel Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people trapped by other people's destinies from a rain-soaked cottage on the Welsh coast.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet Ines performing his nightly ritual at the Hollow Gate, hiding his role behind a quiet life of small kindnesses and a carefully boring routine. His date with Quentin—a warm, curious outsider—goes strangely well until Quentin mentions a dream of a door. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by hope, shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: A Name in Old Ink
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Searching the keepers' archive to reassure himself, Ines finds Quentin's name and face rendered in a prophecy written a hundred years ago, tied to the Veil's renewal. He lies to Quentin about why they can't see each other again. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into obsession as Ines rereads the page all night.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin, hurt by Ines's sudden coldness, follows him to the gate and witnesses the ritual—and the thing pressing against the other side. Ines confesses everything, including the deadline: thirteen lunar turns until the Veil thins. Emotional beat: betrayal transformed into reluctant partnership.

chapters.title: What the Wards Refuse
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The valley's wards begin failing around Quentin specifically, meaning he cannot stay hidden here. Ines decides they must leave for the city of Vael Corrin to consult the exiled mage Sefu Adeyemi, the only scholar of prophecies. Emotional beat: grief for the only home Ines has ever known.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Silence
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. First journey beyond the valley; magic floods back into Quentin's senses painfully, revealing he carries latent power he never chose. They are ambushed by Wardens of the old order who recognize the prophecy-mark. Emotional beat: wonder soured by fear as Quentin realizes everyone wants something from him.

chapters.title: Sefu's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In Vael Corrin, Sefu reveals the prophecy's second half, long suppressed: the 'vessel' it names is meant to be consumed when the Veil renews. Worse, the founding keepers wrote it deliberately. Emotional beat: horror and fury—the justice Ines served his whole life was built on a lie.

chapters.title: The Circle of Strays
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Hunted by both Wardens and a mage faction wanting to use Quentin, the pair gathers fellow outcasts: Sefu, a defected Warden named Bryn, and a half-Veil spirit called Moss. Around a fire, they form an unlikely family. Emotional beat: warmth and belonging discovered precisely because none of them fit anywhere else.

chapters.title: Turn of the Twelfth Moon
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Bryn betrays them under Warden coercion, delivering Quentin to the mage faction, who intend to force the renewal early and burn him out as fuel. Ines chooses rebellion over law, breaking into their sanctum with Sefu and Moss. Emotional beat: rage sharpened into resolve; Ines stops asking permission.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, climax. Beneath the full moon, Quentin stands at the Veil's heart as the faction's ritual tears it wide. Instead of fleeing, he offers the power a choice—mirroring what Ines once offered him: trust freely given. Ines and the circle anchor him. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into agency as Quentin refuses to be anyone's instrument.

chapters.title: Keepers, All of Us
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, resolution. The Veil is remade not as a single gate but distributed among the circle, each carrying a shard—including Quentin, now permanently marked but free. The valley loses its magiclessness; its people must finally see the world whole. Ines and Quentin stay together, no longer invisible. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—justice rewritten by hand, home redefined as people, not walls.
